intended_object: The standard bijection between the free group on one generator (a type with exactly one element) and the integers ℤ. It sends a reduced word to its exponent sum, and its inverse sends n to the generator raised to the power n. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The forward map is `sum (map 1 x)`. Here `map 1` sends every generator to `1 : ℤ`, so it maps `FreeGroup α` into `FreeGroup ℤ`. Then `sum` adds up the letters, so the result is the exponent sum of the word, which is the usual isomorphism with ℤ. The inverse is `n ↦ of default ^ n`. The two inverse laws are proved, so the definition really is a bijection, and it is the standard one.

The only hypothesis is `[Unique α]`, which is the natural setting: any one-element generating type, not just `Unit`. This makes it a generalization of the existing `FreeGroup.freeGroupUnitEquivInt`, which is the same bijection for `Unit`. The group structure is added in the same file by `FreeGroup.mulEquivIntOfUnique`, an isomorphism with `Multiplicative ℤ` built on this definition, so stating this one as a plain `Equiv` is fine.
